list.title: Email templates
list.description: A template is a message written once and rendered by the API on every send. The send screen names a template by its slug — not by its title — and passes the variables it interpolates.
list.panel_description: Filtering happens here in the browser: this endpoint takes no search parameter and returns the whole set in one call.
list.search_placeholder: Filter by name, slug or subject…
list.copy_failed: The slug could not be copied — this browser blocked the clipboard.
list.caption: Email templates
list.empty_description: Write the subject and the body once, give it a slug, and every send can ask for it by that slug and pass nothing but the variables.
list.delete_body: “{{name}}” is removed for good. Any send that asks for the slug {{slug}} starts failing from that moment on, until another template takes the slug.

editor.title: Edit template
editor.description: Changes take effect on the next send: the API renders the template as it stands when a message is queued.
editor.new_description: Name it, give it a slug, and write the subject and bodies the API will render on every send.
editor.panel_template_description: How this template is identified, and the subject line the recipient sees.
editor.name_hint: Only ever shown in here. Up to 120 characters.
editor.slug_hint: What a send names to reach this template. Derived from the name until you edit it by hand.
editor.description_hint: A note for whoever picks this template later. Up to 400 characters.
editor.description_placeholder: Goes out right after someone signs up.
editor.subject_hint: The subject line. {{example}} placeholders are replaced when the message is sent.
editor.panel_html_description: The rich version of the message. Plain HTML — nothing here is treated as markdown.
editor.html_hint: The recipient's email client is what renders this, so keep the markup conservative — tables and inline styles travel furthest.
editor.panel_text_description: The fallback for clients that do not render HTML — and what a spam filter reads.
editor.text_hint: Sent alongside the HTML; a client that cannot render HTML shows this instead.
editor.panel_variables_description: Every {{example}} placeholder found in the subject and the bodies. A send has to supply a value for each one. This is read from the text as it stands right now, not a list the API publishes.
editor.variables_empty: No {{example}} placeholders in this template yet, so a send needs to pass no variables.
editor.no_body_body: Neither the HTML nor the plain-text body has anything in it, so a send using this template would deliver an empty message. The service refuses to create one that way, and clearing both on an existing template leaves it unusable.
editor.delete_body: “{{name}}” is removed for good. Any send that asks for the slug {{slug}} starts failing from that moment on.
editor.body_required: A template needs at least one body — the service refuses one with neither an HTML nor a plain-text version.
